fixes.explanation: Yes, light. The man says, "He has driven me away and made me walk in darkness instead of light." (Lamentations 3:2) Notice he says he's walking in the darkness, friend. I think this is a man who's tired of not being able to see where he's going.

The text says the opposite, friend. The man says, "He has walled me in so I cannot escape; He has weighed me down with chains." (Lamentations 3:7) He's walled in and weighed down, so slipping out isn't on the table. I think that's a heavy spot to be in.

False is right. The man says, "He has walled me in so I cannot escape; He has weighed me down with chains." (Lamentations 3:7) He says he cannot escape, so he's not slipping out whenever he likes. Walled in and weighed down with chains, and I think that's a heavy spot to be in.

That's what he says. "Even when I cry out and plead for help, He shuts out my prayer." (Lamentations 3:8) He cries out and pleads for help, and he says his prayer is shut out. I think that tells you how much he needs help. It's a heavy line to read.

The verse doesn't say his voice gives out. It says, "Even when I cry out and plead for help, He shuts out my prayer." (Lamentations 3:8) The problem he names is that his prayer is shut out. That's the part that stings.

Right. The man says, "He is a bear lying in wait, a lion hiding in ambush." (Lamentations 3:10) Both animals are waiting and hiding, and that's the picture he chooses. I think it shows how it feels to him, like danger could jump out at any moment. It's a scary thing to say.

A sleeping animal isn't the picture here. The man says, "He is a bear lying in wait, a lion hiding in ambush." (Lamentations 3:10) Those two are waiting and hiding in ambush, and there's no den or sleeping in the verse. I think that's what makes the picture so frightening.
True. He says, "He pierced my kidneys with His arrows." (Lamentations 3:13) It comes right after the bow and the target in verse 12. I think this one hurts, friend, and it's okay to say so.

Hope. The man says, "My strength has perished, along with my hope from the LORD." (Lamentations 3:18) His strength is gone, and he says his hope from the LORD is gone along with it. I think this is the lowest thing he says so far. It's a heavy line, and it's okay to feel that.
